subject: StormPulse: sudden p95/p99 spike — routing & batching mitigations
messages:
From: Tara Nguyen <tara@stormpulse.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden host API latency spike — p95/p99 elevated since 07:00 PST

Hi Alex,

We're seeing a sharp jump in p95/p99 response times and an uptick in 5xxs starting ~07:00 this morning. Our product team noticed timeouts on model.generate calls; the dashboard shows request backlog growth across the cluster.

Quick details:
- Affected region: us-west-2 (our calls default there)
- Impact: degrade on a key feature (summarization) for ~30% of users
- Observable: p95 up from 380ms to ~1.7s, p99 from 720ms to ~3.2s; error rate from 0.1% to 1.6%

We've attached a screenshot of your timestamps and an export of a few server traces. Can you advise immediate mitigations? This is affecting our release demo at 10:30.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Nguyen

T: +1 415-555-0198

Immediate asks while we triage:

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden host API latency spike — p95/p99 elevated since 07:00 PST

Alex / team — I've started correlating serving logs. Early findings:
- A subset of routes (summarize_v2) show sustained KV cache misses and long tail kernel execution (~80-150ms per token) leading to more aggressive batching by the runtime.
- Batching logic is adaptive; with bursty single-token traffic it grew batch windows to reduce cost, but at high concurrency that increased queue depth and p95.
- We also see a small spike in retry traffic from the client SDK between 07:03–07:07 (~12% of total RPS).

Short mitigation options (ranked by speed):
1) Route StormPulse traffic to a higher-priority, less-batched pool (can flip in control plane in <3m).
2) Temporarily reduce max batch window for summarize_v2 and pin batch size to smaller values (requires runtime config push, ~8–12m).
3) Burst dedicated capacity for StormPulse (requires quota check, ~30m to provision).

I'll push logs to the shared drive and attach a condensed excerpt. If customer approves immediate routing change, do it now.

—Sean
Senior Site Reliability Engineer

Attachments: stormpulse_logs_excerpt.zip

Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary & ask for exec approval to grant temporary credits

Team and Tara — quick summary after the routing flip:
- Timing: routing flip completed Mon 18 Jan 09:32 PST. p95 dropped from ~1.7s to ~430ms within 4 minutes; p99 dropped to ~750ms. Error rate returned to baseline.
- Root cause: adaptive batching windows + KV cache churn for summarize_v2 combined with a short client-side retry surge. The runtime's larger batch windows increased queue depth and amplified tail latency under concurrency.
- Permanent fix items:
  * Adjust default batch window heuristics for single-token-heavy routes (SRE): rollout R2027.1.5
  * Add per-route batching profiles in the console (Product/Runtime): tracked in JIRA INF-1137
  * Add client SDK guidance to back off deterministic retry bursts (Docs): DOCS-224

Ask / executive items:
- Customer impact was ~2.5 hours of degraded UX; StormPulse requests temporary account credits (they indicated this on the call). We recommend approving a modest usage credit (commercial to review).
- Recommend an immediate small increase in dedicated buffer (1x burst slice) for priority routing tests for the next 72 hours (ops to provision).

I've attached the condensed logs and the dashboard snapshot for leadership review. If leadership signs off on the credits + buffer, we will: provision the buffer (ETA 30m) and apply the credit within one billing cycle.

—Neha Kapoor
Director, SRE
Redwood Inference
